sources.title: Surfaces From Contours: The Correspondence and Branching Problems
sources.authors: David Meyers, Shelley Skinner, Kenneth Sloan
sources.access: Primary conference full-text PDF accessed, nine pages
sources.locators: PDF pp1-2, printed pp246-247, definitions of contour/section and correspondence ambiguity
sources.established: Contours are surface-plane intersections; sparse contour data has correspondence/topology ambiguity.
sources.difference: Reconstructs surfaces from multiple sections; does not establish a unique solid from our single image or certify a fluorophore observation model.

sources.title: CrossSDF: 3D Reconstruction of Thin Structures From Cross-Sections
sources.access: Primary author preprint HTML full text accessed
sources.locators: Section3.1 Input and output; Section3.2; Section3.4
sources.established: Uses supplied planes and segmented contours to constrain a three-dimensional signed-distance representation; inside/outside information matters.
sources.difference: Its planes are part of input; our unmeasured horizontal slice height is existentially eliminated for a necessary test rather than estimated by neural reconstruction.

sources.title: Validation of three-dimensional diffraction contrast tomography reconstructions by means of electron backscatter diffraction characterization
sources.access: Primary publisher full-text PDF accessed, six pages
sources.established: Unknown cutting-plane orientation must be addressed in geometric validation; near-tangent boundaries amplify section-contour errors.
sources.difference: Materials tomography uses matched pores to estimate planes; it does not validate our biological plane or fluorescence segmentation.

sources.title: Computational reconstruction of cell and tissue surfaces for modeling and data analysis
sources.access: Primary author manuscript full-text PMC HTML accessed; later repeated find encountered browser challenge
sources.locators: Abstract and Introduction, paragraphs on segmented confocal/two-photon stacks and lower out-of-plane resolution
sources.established: Reconstruction is based on microscopy segmentation and must address resolution-dependent geometric artifacts.
sources.difference: Uses volumetric microscopy data; cannot turn a single dark annulus into known three-dimensional tissue occupancy.
